# Organize the content and the functions

This file is step 2 of 5 of the skill `design-interface`.

## Pages

- You sort content or functions into groups. Read [Organization](../../../references/categorization.md).
- You name a section, a link, a heading, or a function. Read [Labeling](../../../references/labeling.md).
- You design how people move between screens. Read [Navigation](../../../references/navigation.md).
- You add or change the search of a product. Read [Search system](../../../references/search-system.md).
- You write a label, a message, or an instruction in an interface. Read [UX writing](../../../references/ux-writing.md).
- You design for a specific operating system or with its components. Read [Platform conventions](../../../references/platform-conventions.md).
- You build a control, a form, a text style, a color choice, or media. Read [Accessibility](../../../references/accessibility.md).

## Directives

- Show only the content and the controls that the current task needs. ^show-what-the-task-needs
- Run a card sort with users before you choose the categories of a new structure. ^card-sort-new-categories
- Name each category in words that users recognize. ^name-categories-for-users
- Review each category name from a card sort before you use it as a label. ^review-card-sort-names
- Define a controlled vocabulary for the content of each product. ^define-controlled-vocabulary
- Use one word for one meaning in each interface. ^one-word-one-meaning
- Use the words of the users in each label and message, not internal terms. ^use-the-words-of-users
- Make each heading and label state the topic or the purpose of its content. ^descriptive-headings-and-labels
- Give each page a title that states its topic or purpose. ^descriptive-page-title
- State the purpose of each link in its text or in the sentence that holds it. ^link-purpose
- Give components with the same function the same label and the same glyph on each page. ^consistent-identification
- Keep repeated navigation elements in the same relative order on each screen. ^keep-navigation-order
- Show the current location of the user in the navigation. ^show-current-location
- Give `2` or more ways to reach each page, unless the page is a step in a process. ^two-ways-to-each-page
- Use a tab bar or a navigation bar only for navigation, not for actions. ^tabs-for-navigation
- Give each destination in a tab bar or a navigation bar a text label. ^label-each-tab

## Branches

If a heading matches the work, follow each directive under it.

### If the target is an Apple device

- Keep each tab bar item visible and enabled, even when its content is not available. ^apple-keep-tabs-enabled

### If the target is Android

- Give a navigation bar `3` to `5` destinations. ^navigation-bar-destinations
